name: How the Tower Sat Down
subject: settlement_lothal

levels.prompt: At the foot of the standing wall, the dressed blocks do not fan outward as a fallen tower should. Their courses continue down into the slope, storey laid over storey beneath your feet.
levels.entry: Twenty-two storeys in the chronicles. Four here, and a great deal of rubble that is not shaped like rubble.

levels.prompt: Follow one course past the broken corner. The joints keep their intervals all the way into the silt.
levels.entry: The fallen stone lies in courses. It did not scatter -- it descended.

levels.prompt: Think of the dockyard reef, then look at the foot of the wall. The line where the ground meets the stone sits strangely high.
levels.entry: The delta took the foundation before anything took the walls. The tower sank into its own footing and the upper structure came through the lower.

levels.prompt: Look from the square corner still standing to the water lying beyond it. The corner has kept its shape. The delta has not.
levels.entry: Kavik built for a delta that drained. After the Shattering it stopped draining. The tower did not fail; the ground under it changed its mind.

notes: Opens the stair shaft. The reading is deliberately sympathetic to Kavik -- the building was sound and the world moved.
